item.title: Let it begin. Also, dream a little bigger.
item.content:encoded:
This article definitely needs to be expounded upon. I will.

As to the blood, it's redacted because it probably isn't blood from any common, ordinary thing. The fact that it's mentioned in the containment procedures, though, means that it likely has implications for SCP-938's containment, to be considered by those who must consider. Those staffing Capacitor Bank 0, or maybe more generally working at BCRS-07.

It could be SCP-1000 blood, but you wouldn't want to just up and state that in the general writeup, or else you have, firstly, told people who do not necessarily need to be aware that SCP-1000 exists that it does, and secondly, have told them some of what it is, and given them a lot to consider about what that might mean.

That's not to say that it is SCP-1000 blood. This was written some time before SCP-1000. But that'd be pretty damn creepy, if it was, huh? Considering what this seems to be, and what SCP-1000 is about.

In either case, if this is loose, there are going to be much more significant concerns than the flavor of punch on tap. It will be a significant concern again once it's caught, but not until, and currently, it is.

So that's why it's redacted, in-universe and out, and why it's mentioned in the containment procedures.

item.title: Re: A watery explanation
item.content:encoded:
Did the math. You need to know the voltage your capacitor supports to be able to convert farads to joules.
Your entity's energy is 513 megajoules.
An industrial capacitor (I chose EPCOS B4345, because it was frequently mentioned) can store around 1200 joules. Ergo, 427 500 capacitors, around 2 kg each. That's a train load of'em.
Russian К75-100 can offer the 19kJ you mention, but they're 33kg each. Also a train load.

item.title: Re: A watery explanation
item.content:encoded: There's no current, but that capacitor is still storing energy, which can be measured in joules. While technically incorrect, it's much easier to list the energy stored by the capacitor than it is to crunch the numbers to figure out how many capacitors of whatever number of farads it would take to contain it, especially when said conversions make it apparent that this thing is in actuality impossible to contain. But, that doesn't fly around here, so I fudged some terms and some numbers to make it seem plausible without a completely absurd expenditure of resources.

item.title: A watery explanation
item.content:encoded:
Joules are energy. "Passing an electric current of one ampere through a resistance of one ohm for one second", to quote the almighty Wikipedia.
When a charge is stored in a capacitor, there's no current.
Imagine a water tower. When filled with water, it has the potential to create a flow of water. Same goes for a charged capacitor - it has a potential to create an electrical flow.
When you open the valve, water starts flowing and you have a current. The speed at which water flows through the pipe is roughly the equivalent of an ampere. The energy the water flows with is enough to propel the water at a given speed. That's Joules.
Farads, in this case, are the amount of water that can be stored in this tower.

Focus on the point you are trying to make or the reaction you want to get from the reader, and cut out or move anything that does not promote that reaction even if it is perfectly logical. You're more than good enough at writing out the kind of documentation a top secret science conspiracy would write, you need to switch gears to story-telling disguised as documentation.

Make your containment procedures much simpler but keep in the part about the presence of blood being perfectly normal — that is fantastic first step in setting the mood — then tell us what the thing is in as concise a description as possible. It's a hostile energy being that is incredibly hard to contain due to its nature. its motives are inscrutable and it is capable of doing a lot more damage than it is currently doing. Ditch anything in the description that doesn't convey that point directly. Then hit the reader with the final twist, where this thing creatively murdered its protected target by staging a false emergency call prior to triggering an actual heart attack.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
Regarding "things what make you crazy": I think that sometimes, because we're so conditioned to watch out for this, people assume TWMYC is the situation every time an SCP causes mental problems. As far as I can see, there's two ways SCP-induced crazyness goes:

Type A: Primary Effect Insanity
-A Type A effect is the direct effect of the SCP, for example, SCP-AAA is a deck of cards that makes you depressed. That is exactly its effect, the insanity caused defines why it is an SCP. Generally, Type A insanity is a sign of bad writing.

Type B: Secondary Effect Insanity
-A Type B effect is extrapolated from exposure to the SCP, i.e. the SCP does not make you insane, the knowledge of it does. For example, SCP-BBB is a DVD that shows you how you will die. It doesn't physically make you insane, but that knowledge could be bad for your mental health. Generally, Type B insanity is a sign of, if not good writing, at least not bad writing.

Basically, I think the issue is that whenever people see insanity of any kind in an SCP, they assume that it's Type A.

Nusquam wanted awareness of it to begin a few decades ago, I assumed (taking into account the fact that the Foundation's been following this thing for ages before containment became feasible) that the very first place they would build would a) be a prototype for the future and b) Be used on this thing. It does not inflate the importance of the SCP, it makes sense (to me).

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
as it's a blatant attempt to inflate the importance of your SCP

No, it's not.

Do you really need that much technobabble to explain how it infiltrates a house and electrocutes individuals?

What can I cut while still giving the reader a clear indication of how dangerous the entity is at a given time?

Does it really need to "hunt" certain individuals, making them paranoid in the process?

With the motive I've got in mind for it, yes, it would hunt specific individuals. However, there's no way for the Foundation to know this motive, so I don't specify it.

(Besides, that just borders on "things what make people go crazy".)

This does not drive ordinary people crazy "because lol." If you knew or suspected you were being followed at all times, and furthermore believed you saw things which showed up in no photograph, you might be a tad bit unsettled.

It's not a comprehensive explanation of how something is contained, it's a quick and dirty briefing in case something goes horribly wrong and we need to know RIGHT NOW how to make sure something is safely contained.

If it gets out of the capacitor bank, you're in for some fun any way you cut it. That's why the containment procedures are so thorough - to ensure this doesn't happen. There's no "quick and dirty" containment stratagem for 500MJ of electrical energy.

item.title: (no title)
item.content:encoded:
"Capacitor Bank Zero"? "Warehouse Zero"? I'm going to have to say that many people frown upon that kind of naming, as it's a blatant attempt to inflate the importance of your SCP by trying to imply that it's somehow "the original" or "the secret", much like "Patient Zero".

Aside from that, the article seems to suffer from being a bit long and meanders through several side topics that don't seem to help the basic concept. Do you really need that much technobabble to explain how it infiltrates a house and electrocutes individuals? Does it really need to "hunt" certain individuals, making them paranoid in the process? (Besides, that just borders on "things what make people go crazy".) Do you really need the association with St. Elmo's Fire?

Finally, the Special Containment Procedures section is far too long. It's not a comprehensive explanation of how something is contained, it's a quick and dirty briefing in case something goes horribly wrong and we need to know RIGHT NOW how to make sure something is safely contained. Try to keep it at two paragraphs or less if at all possible.
